SCIENCE
THE CURRICULUM
Boys learn best by doing.
Pilgrims’ scientists are recognised by senior schools for their confidence, practical skills and strong understanding of theory. Our curriculum blends hands-on learning with theory, making science relevant and engaging. By Year 8, boys are confident scientists, often working at GCSE-level practical standard.
In the Lower Prep, science is taught through an investigative approach, helping boys develop skills in the scientific method through prediction, experimentation and evaluation, supported by Forest School in Year 3.
From Year 5 onwards, boys study biology, chemistry and physics as separate subjects, learning in fully equipped laboratories with support from a dedicated lab technician to combine practical skills with theory.
Humanities
Humanities at Pilgrims’ inspires curiosity about the world, developing boys’ understanding of people, places and the past through engaging, hands-on learning.
French
Boys are encouraged to engage with authentic French, developing both confidence and enjoyment of the language.
Mathematics
At Pilgrims’, we encourage boys to become confident, independent thinkers who can question, reason and check their own work.

FRENCH
More than je m’appelle
le programme d’études français
Boys are encouraged to read, listen and engage with authentic French, developing both enjoyment of the language and the ability to hold conversations with native speakers. A strong balance is maintained between grammar and spoken confidence, with boys encouraged to take risks in both writing and speaking. Learning is supported through songs, games, role-play and enrichment activities such as a French film club.
We use a bespoke curriculum, drawing on the Expo scheme, with pupils working ahead of national levels. By Year 8, most grammar is covered, preparing boys for senior school and future study.
At the top of the school, advanced work develops higher-level skills, including translation, discussion and complex grammar through engaging texts. Native speakers are supported with differentiated work and opportunities to further develop their skills, including informal French-speaking events.
There’s a real focus on a fully rounded education for the boys. There’s not just music, not just sport and not just academic focus – it’s really everything. And that’s important.
SPECIALIST LANGUAGE PRACTICE IN YEAR 8
The French curriculum is further enhanced in Year 8 by a weekly intervention from a specialist language teacher. The boys will work individually or in small groups to sharpen and enhance their speaking and grammatical skills. This further reinforces the notion that language is often a communication tool used on a smaller scale. Everyone gets to make progress at their own rate and, like learning any language, often it is the mistakes that we make which help us learn the most effectively.

English is the fundamental to all learning and at Pilgrims’ we provide a thorough grounding in all aspects of literacy.
All boys are encouraged to read and there are plenty of opportunities to explore the world of books.

HUMANITIES
Open minds, wide worlds
GEOGRAPHY
There’s never been a more important time to study Geography. An awareness of the changing climate, social, economic and physical issues is crucial for a better understanding of the world. Debate and discussion are a big part of geography at The Pilgrims’ School. We place a keen emphasis on the ability to empathise with people in different situations and environments around the world.
Geography at Pilgrims’ equips boys with a wide range of skills, from map reading and data analysis to independent research and understanding global cultures and environments.
The curriculum covers key topics such as rivers and coasts, weather and climate, tectonics, population, and sustainability, all designed to encourage connections between subjects and real-world experience.
Learning is highly practical, with regular fieldwork and trips. With the River Itchen, water meadows and the South Downs National Park on the doorstep, boys benefit from rich, hands-on exploration of the world around them.
Achievement in the humanities is high. Pupils are notably articulate and they apply their speaking and listening skills confidently in lessons and discussions. They listen with care to the thoughts and opinions of their peers, happily sharing ideas.
HISTORY
Set among Roman and medieval history in the heart of ancient Wessex, Pilgrims’ offers a rich and inspiring environment for young historians. Boys are encouraged to question, explore and understand the past, building a strong foundation of key events, people and places.
We study Imperial China and world History from Year 3. Learning is brought to life through regular trips and hands-on experiences, including visits to historic sites such as Portchester Castle, Fishbourne Roman Villa and Portsmouth Historic Dockyard, as well as access to the Winchester College Treasury. GENERAL STUDIES
Critical thinking, or ‘General Studies’, is the study of all aspects of the world around us, including politics, ethics, culture, technology.
Boys are taught to question, debate, speculate – to think for themselves.
Critical thinking begins for with a focus on verbal and non-verbal reasoning for younger boys.
n Year 6, we move on to study different human qualities, using, for example, Beowulf and Anne Frank to spark discussions about character traits, motivation, and individual and collective responsibility.
Some of the boys will sit a general paper in their final exam. For these boys in Year 8, critical thinking enables them to construct a discursive argument in response to a question about, for example, the merits of democracy, or the artistic value of modern art.
Through critical thinking, boys are taught to value the power and protocol of written and spoken argument, and to draw their own conclusions.
They may end up seeing the world differently. They certainly become thinkers.

Latin
Latin is not a dead language at Pilgrims’
In and out of the classroom
The study of Latin is introduced in Year 6. You might be surprised to know that it’s one of our most popular subjects. Greek is offered as a Commoner after school activity.
Literature and Classical Civilisation
Alongside their linguistic studies, all year groups explore Homer’s The Iliad and Odyssey in translation. Knowledge of these key texts is required at Common Entrance and the boys love listening to scenes from these epic poems. There are also opportunities to learn about:
Roman daily life
Life in the Roman army
The history of Roman Britain
Ancient Greek
Ancient Greek is offered as part of the syllabus in Year 8. We begin by learning the alphabet and progress to reading and translating stories. Working at their own pace, some boys will tackle Ancient Greek scholarship papers, others do the Ancient Greek Common Entrance paper at Level 1 or Level 2. More often than not, boys study Ancient Greek purely to add to their general knowledge.
There’s a real focus on a fully rounded education for the boys. There’s not just music, not just sport and not just academic focus – it’s really everything. And that’s important.

All boys are encouraged to read and there are plenty of opportunities to explore the world of books.

Music and choir at Pilgrims’ play a central role in school life, offering boys outstanding opportunities to develop their musical talent, perform with confidence and be part of a rich choral tradition.
French

MATHEMATICS
Inspiring curiosity, logic, creativity, and discovery
THE CURRICULUM
At Pilgrims’, we encourage boys to become confident, independent thinkers who can question, reason and check their own work. We see maths as a way of thinking, aiming to make it engaging, relevant and challenging while equipping boys with the skills to understand and apply it in the real world.
Teaching focuses on building confidence to analyse, make connections and draw conclusions, rather than simply finding the right answer. From the outset, strong numeracy skills are developed, allowing greater focus on deeper thinking as boys progress.
Boys are set to ensure the right level of challenge, working across numbers, measures, shapes, graphs and statistics, with algebra becoming increasingly important as they move through the school.
Pilgrims’ is almost uniquely placed in the UK. Close to being a specialist music school whilst not being one, and having all the advantages of sport and a wider academic education.
There’s a real focus on a fully rounded education for the boys. There’s not just music, not just sport and not just academic focus – it’s really everything. And that’s important.
Pilgrims' is an absolutely fantastic school with the most incredible and dedicated teachers. My son is nurtured and encouraged, in all the right amounts. The staff really understand my son and genuinely really care.
Pilgrims’ gives each boy a love of learning.
NATIONAL COMPETITIONS
Boys in Years 5 and 6 can take part in the Primary Maths Challenge and the Junior Maths Challenge, organised by the Mathematical Association.
Both are national competitions that allow the boys to pit their wits against other pupils across the country and to win awards for their mathematical prowess.

A Welcome From
our headmaster
“At Thorngrove School, we are proud to offer a warm, nurturing, and family-oriented environment where children aged 2½ to 13 can thrive. From the very start of their journey in our exceptional Nursery, each child is supported and inspired to reach their full potential.
Our architect-designed buildings are set within 25 acres of beautiful grounds, providing the perfect setting for learning, exploration, and growth. We are committed to delivering an outstanding education, exceptional pastoral care, and a truly enriching experience for every child who becomes part of the Thorngrove community.”

SEE FOR YOURSELF
BOOK A TOUR
Discover the charm of Thorngrove School, where education meets nature in a stunning countryside setting. Our beautiful grounds, rich with greenery and wildlife, provide the perfect environment for curiosity, creativity, and growth. Come and experience the warmth of our community, explore our exceptional facilities, and see firsthand how we inspire young minds.
our AIMS
Be Curious
Curiosity is at the heart of learning. We provide consistently excellent and exciting teaching which enables every pupil to develop intellectual enquiry. Our aim is to ignite and nurture a lifelong love of learning. These efforts build upon our unchanged founding pillars: Inspiration, Confidence, and Achievement
Be Community-Minded
Encouraging sensitivity and empathy is key to our approach. We help pupils develop these qualities towards those around them and in the wider world. Additionally, we actively promote well-being, mindfulness, and a strong sense of worth in all our pupils.
Be Challenged
At Thorngrove, we are dedicated to helping every child achieve their full potential. This means maximising academic results in all internal, standardised, and external examinations. Beyond academics, we focus on building resilience and promoting a positive mind-set among all our pupils.
Be Creative
We believe in enabling pupils, regardless of their ability, to discover and develop their individual talents. This includes a wide range of activities such as Sport, the Performing and Creative Arts, and other enriching pursuits. Our goal is to provide opportunities for every child to shine.
“A wide range of extra-curricular activities provide pupils with enjoyable and meaningful learning experiences. This is a significant strength of the school. Wrap-around care & Holiday Clubs
What's in this section?
At Thorngrove we understand that some parents need ‘wrap-around’ care to allow for their busy working lifestyle.
We run a Breakfast Club Monday to Thursday from 7.30am. Pupils can be dropped off at the New Hall where they are looked after by a member of staff and offered a selection of toast, cereals, fruit and eggs for breakfast.
In the afternoon, we run an aftercare facility which is available every day after school. It is located in the Old Hall and supervised by member of Thorngrove staff. The children will be given a snack to keep them going. They have many toys, games and activities available to them. The Aftercare facility starts at 3.15pm in the afternoon and finishes at 5.30pm. For more information about the cost of Breakfast Club and Aftercare, please ask the school office.
Holiday Club is also very popular, and we have teamed up with SuperCamps to enable us to offer clubs during every half-term and holiday. SuperCamps create fun and interesting activities to keep the children entertained, even on wet days! For more information please visit the SuperCamps website (link below) or pop into the school office.

Sports Curriculum
What's in this section?
At Thorngrove, we believe Games and PE are important for developing mental well-being as well as physical fitness, team work, resilience and social skills.
Sport is an integral part of the education we offer. Our ‘sports for all’ philosophy ensures that every child enjoys regular exercise and the experience of learning new sports.
All pupils from nursery to year 8 have regular PE and games lessons with specialist teachers. For pupils in years 3 to 8 weekly matches against a range of local prep schools take place on Wednesday and Friday afternoons. A wide variety of lunchtime and after-school sports clubs also take place, including (but not limited to) football, rugby, netball, hockey, cross-country, ballet, cricket, tennis, and judo.
Our sporting curriculum is designed to foster physical awareness, mental wellbeing, team spirit, an understanding of getting out of life what you put in, as well as learning to lose and win with good grace. Frequently on the athletics track the loudest cheers are for those who are coming in last or who pick themselves up from a fall and carry on!
Thorngrove has an enviable record of sporting achievements at local and regional level, but whether your child is naturally sporty or not, they will be taught by specialist teachers from an early age and will be included in regular house and inter-school matches. They will be encouraged to enjoy sport and maintain an active lifestyle during their time at Thorngrove and beyond. The Sports Department also takes regular tours in the UK and abroad – most recently a football and hockey tour to Valencia.

Performing Arts
What's in this section?
Thorngrove is renowned for its Performing Arts programme. Children are exposed to drama, dance and music at an early age and enjoy performing in front of their peers and parents on a regular basis.
Music is at the heart of the school and Thorngrove takes immense pride in its outstanding musical achievements, showcasing the talent and dedication of our pupils. Over the years, our music program has nurtured a vast range of musical abilities, from gifted solo performers to harmonious ensembles.
Not only do pupils shine in the traditional domains of classical music, but they also embrace contemporary genres, demonstrating versatility and creativity. Our music faculty, coupled with a supportive learning environment and a wonderful team of peripatetic teachers, has propelled our students to reach remarkable heights, embodying true musical excellence.
Drama and the performing arts are a hugely popular part of school life. Children are exposed to drama at an early age and perform in front of their peers and parents on a regular basis. Drama is taught as part of the English curriculum and from Year 3 as a separate subject by a specialist drama teacher.
Every child has the opportunity to be in productions whilst at Thorngrove. These have included The Little Mermaid, Matilda, Shrek and The Lion King.
Throughout the year, trips are arranged to local theatres, including the Watermill (with whom we are a partner school) and national theatres, including The Globe and theatres in the West End.
LAMDA Speech and Drama lessons are extremely popular with exams being held on the school site each term. We are proud that our pupils have enjoyed remarkable success in this field.

ISI Inspection Reports
What's in this section?
Rare "Significant strength" awarded
Thorngrove School was inspected by the Independent Schools Inspectorate (ISI) on behalf of the Department for Education from 11th-13th June 2024.
This inspection was part of the new Framework for inspections introduced in September 2023 which has moved away from graded judgements. ‘Framework 23’ places an emphasis on pupil voice and wellbeing and allows the inspectors to spend extended time with pupils and gain a deeper understanding of the schools they visit.
Thorngrove was found to have met the standard in all areas which is the highest grade possible under ‘Framework 23’.
The standards focused on are:
The inspecting team were quickly able to recognise the positive influence that Thorngrove has on the pupils’ development across the board. Extra-curricular provision comes in for particular praise, being identified as a ‘significant strength’ of the school. “The wide range of extra-curricular activities that provide the pupils with enjoyable and meaningful experiences.” The ISI rarely denotes a ‘significant strength’ in its reports, and the bar is set extremely high – any such provision must result in a clear, demonstrable and highly-beneficial impact for pupils. We are incredibly proud to receive this exceptional accolade, currently only awarded to 16% of inspected Prep Schools in the country.

Enrichment and Clubs
What's in this section?
Introduced in 2022 the Thorngrove ‘Be’ Programme is designed to provide pupils with a broader range of experiences and help to develop their character, providing them with opportunities to further harness skills that will allow them to flourish in 21st Century life.
The programme focusses on four key strands which align with the Aims of the school:
Pupils spend the afternoon every Tuesday undertaking activities within one of these areas.
The world is a large and diverse place, and we think it is important that pupils are exposed to this in a productive and thought-provoking way.
As a school we are also committed to developing the character of the pupils within the school. Greater exposure to a wider range of opportunities will help them develop core skills such as collaboration, perseverance, problem solving and communication, all of which enable them to develop as well-rounded individuals.
A variety of clubs are also available to pupils throughout the year. The activities vary widely and children can choose to be in as many or as few as they want. They take place at lunch break and after school and the full list of clubs is published at the start of each term.
Most activities are free to do apart from ballet, judo and street dance.
A current list of activities is available from the school office.

The Creative Arts
What's in this section?
ART
Art is an important part of life at Thorngrove. We provide a rich and varied curriculum which fosters curiosity, resourcefulness and creativity, alongside the acquisition of technical skills in drawing, painting, sculpture and printing.
In weekly Art lessons, children learn to select, use and manipulate materials and media for particular effects, making creative choices for their own work. They investigate artworks and explore styles, approaches and techniques used in contemporary and traditional practice, celebrating the diversity of Art and developing visual literacy.
Many additional opportunities in Art are offered through our extracurricular programmes and scholarship groups. Pottery, Photography and Textiles are amongst the courses included in a wide selection of Art clubs and Enrichment projects. At Thorngrove, we aim to nurture a lifelong love of Art and give children the experiences needed to successfully express their creative ideas and become confident artists of the future.
D&T
D&T is taught in a spacious and well-equipped workshop. Pupils are able to discover the different stages of a design process and the various tools, materials and techniques required to turn their dreams and ideas into reality.
There is hardly anything more fulfilling for a pupil than to produce a quality item with their own imagination and their own hands: a rewarding tangible three-dimensional proof of their ability. Tools are introduced carefully, and every student has a chance to practise before embarking on their main projects. Confidence in tool handling is built up progressively and more tools, machines and materials become available to the pupils throughout their time here. We focus on a huge variety of project work incorporating traditional techniques and modern technology such as the laser cutter to cut, etch and engrave.
Thorngrove is continually investing in Design and Technology as we believe it is a vital part of the creative programme.

Pastoral Care
What's in this section?
At Thorngrove, we pride ourselves on our outstanding pastoral care. Family is at the heart of our ethos, and we like to think of the school as an extension of each child’s family.
When a child joins Thorngrove, their form teacher is their first point of pastoral contact. The form teacher plays a vital role in helping children settle into their new environment—supporting them in building friendships, becoming familiar with daily routines and feeling secure both inside and outside the classroom. With small classes across the school, teachers get to know the children well, understanding what makes them tick, their interests and their ambitions. Form teachers are also the first port of call for parents with any queries.
In addition to the form teacher, each pupil is supported by a Head of Section, who has overarching responsibility for their pastoral and academic welfare during their time in that part of the school. Heads of Section work closely with form teachers on a daily basis to ensure that all pupils are happy, confident, and thriving.
Our Heads of Section are:
Beyond this, we have a dedicated and experienced wellbeing team that includes a qualified School Counsellor, two trained Emotional Literacy Support Assistants (ELSAs), and a number of paediatric first aid-trained staff across the school—including in the office and our teaching assistant team. Children have access to both emotional and physical care throughout the school day. Our Medical Room supports children with any bumps or bruises they may sustain, while The Snug offers a calm, quiet space for those who may be feeling overwhelmed or need time to regulate their emotions.
Our Year 8 pupils, guided by the staff, also take on leadership roles as ‘buddies’ to the younger children. They help during morning registration, they play together at break times, and provide ongoing support throughout the week. This fosters a culture of care and responsibility and sets a positive example for the whole school community. Pupil voice is highly valued at Thorngrove. Our active School Council includes representatives from every year group (Reception to Year 8) and provides a forum for meaningful discussion, inclusion, and change. The Council plays an important role in shaping school life, with many initiatives and ideas coming directly from the children themselves.
Another important layer of pastoral support comes from our Heads of House. Every child at Thorngrove belongs to one of four Houses - Ash, Beech, Oak or Rowan - and remains in their House throughout their time at the school. These Houses nurture a sense of family, teamwork, healthy competition, and friendship. House meetings take place regularly each term and contribute significantly to the school’s supportive, community spirit.
Pastoral care at Thorngrove is overseen by our Senior Deputy Head (Pastoral), Mr Tom Layton, who meets regularly with staff to discuss any concerns and ensure that each child’s needs are fully understood and supported. These regular meetings help us maintain a well-rounded, consistent picture of the children in our care. At Thorngrove, we are proud to be a warm, welcoming, and close-knit school community. We believe that feeling safe, known, and valued is the foundation for every child to flourish.

Directors
What's in this section?
Thorngrove School was founded in 1988 by Nick and Connie Broughton. After several years of teaching in London, they chose to move to the beautiful Hampshire countryside to start their family and establish a school rooted in warmth, ambition, and community.
Thanks to its success and unique atmosphere, Thorngrove flourished and grew year on year. There are currently over 200 pupils at the school.
In the summer of 2009, Nick and Connie stepped back from the day-to-day running of the school to take up their roles as Directors, appointing their Deputy Head, Adam King, as Headmaster. In September 2022, Adam was succeeded by Nick Graham, who assumed the role following five years as Senior Deputy Head. The Broughtons remain very much part of daily life at Thorngrove. They are often seen walking their dogs, Raffy and Rory, around the grounds and continue to take a genuine interest in the happiness and well-being of every child.
In September 2022, the Broughtons appointed a Board of Directors consisting of eight members (see list below).
Nick Broughton - Director and Chair of the Board
Nick founded Thorngrove School with his wife, Connie, in 1988 on their family farm, with the vision of creating a nurturing and family-focused education for their four children.
He studied Mathematics at the University of East Anglia and began his career as a lecturer at Newbury College of Further Education, later teaching in London where he met Connie. The couple then moved to Barcelona to teach English as a foreign language before returning to Newbury, where Nick taught at Barton Peveril Sixth Form College.
After five years running the family farm, Nick combined his passion for education and community to establish Thorngrove, which has since grown into the thriving school it is today.
Connie Broughton - Director and Secretary
Connie co-founded Thorngrove with her husband, Nick, in 1988, and together they led the school until 2009. Alongside her leadership role, she was a dedicated form teacher and taught Latin to the older pupils. Connie studied Spanish and French at London University and went on to teach both subjects in senior schools before moving to Highclere, where the idea of founding a school first took shape.
In 2023, she published a book about the founding of Thorngrove entitled ‘An Interesting Experiment’, with proceeds supporting the Brain Tumour Charity. Connie takes great pride in the fact that all four of her children – and now ten grandchildren – have attended, or are currently attending, Thorngrove.
James Broughton - Director
James graduated from Goldsmiths College, London with a BA Ed Hons degree and began his career teaching Design and Technology at an SEN school in London. He later returned to Newbury, the area where he grew up, and is now proud to have two sons at Thorngrove.
Passionate about hands-on learning, James helped introduce both beekeeping and pig husbandry to the school. He also enjoys putting his DIY skills to use behind the scenes, building sets for Thorngrove’s ambitious school productions.
Jessica Thomas - Director responsible for Health and Safety
Jessica graduated from the University of Bristol with a BA Hons in Classics, before completing an MA in Ceramics. She began her career in publishing, working for several years as an editor at Penguin Random House, before relocating to the countryside to raise her three children.
In 2016, she retrained as a teacher and is now Thorngrove’s Head of Latin. In addition to leading the department, she contributes to the school’s broader cultural life through the creative and performing arts enrichment programmes.
Jessica also serves as Director with responsibility for Health and Safety, ensuring the highest standards of care and compliance across the school.
Bryony Wingfield Digby - Director responsible for Safeguarding
Bryony studied Sculpture at the University of Leeds before completing her PGCE in Art and Design at the University of Brighton. She later gained a CELTA qualification and spent two exciting years teaching English as a Foreign Language in Buenos Aires. A practising artist, she has taught at Marlborough College and now at St Edward’s, where she continues to share her love of creativity with young people.
As a former Thorngrove pupil herself, Bryony is delighted to have come full circle and return as Director. With all three of her children now happily at Thorngrove, she feels especially proud to be part of the school community once again.
Miranda Price - Director
Miranda graduated from Cardiff University with a BA (Hons) in Ancient History before completing a PGCE specialising in Early Years. She spent many years as a Nursery Teacher at a Prep School in Dulwich before joining Thorngrove in 2012 to lead the Nursery.
Now an integral member of the Pre-Prep team, Miranda is often the first point of contact for new Thorngrove families. She is a firm believer in the school’s ethos and values, which she promotes while caring for the youngest children. With both of her children attending Thorngrove, Miranda is a passionate and active member of the whole school community.
Charlotte Fraser - Non-Executive Director
Charlotte Fraser is a Thorngrove parent and has been a director since 2022. Charlotte read Modern Languages at Brasenose College, Oxford. She then trained as a lawyer and is a Partner at Farrer & Co, where she runs the firm's Contentious Trusts and Estates team.
Gareth Jones - Non-Executive Director
With an English with History degree and a Masters in Educational Leadership, Gareth is an experienced and passionate educationalist who has worked in the prep sector for over 25 years. He started his career at the Dragon School in Oxford where, among many things, he was Director of Sport, Director of the Extended Curriculum, a Housemaster and Chair of the Common Room. From there he spent six years as Head of St Andrew’s Prep in Eastbourne before moving, in 2021, to Bilton Grange in Warwickshire, as Headmaster. Bilton Grange is part of the Rugby School Group and Gareth’s role includes being part of the Executive Leadership Team for the Group which now has several schools in the UK as well as a growing number overseas.
An active member of IAPS, the organisation that supports prep schools, Gareth has sat on both the sports and pastoral committees and is co-chair of one of their school networks. He was a governor of a state infant school before joining Thorngrove in a non-executive Director role, in September 2022.

Nursery
What's in this section?
Thorngrove Nursery – where confidence and creativity shine!
At Thorngrove, we welcome children from the age of two and a half into a nurturing and inspiring environment. Set within two vibrant, cosy, and happy rooms, our youngest children settle quickly, feeling right at home - allowing their confidence, curiosity, and creativity to flourish.
Our Nursery is situated within the main school building, complete with a dedicated outdoor space and a direct link to the Reception classroom. This thoughtful layout supports high levels of attainment and ensures a smooth, natural transition into the next stage of their learning journey.
Children benefit from the full range of Thorngrove’s beautiful facilities, regularly enjoying the woodlands, school grounds, and eco spaces. They also have access to specialist teaching in French, P.E., Ballet, Music, and Forest School - enriching their experiences and broadening their horizons from an early age.
We are especially proud of the way our environment, teaching, and carefully planned activities positively shape our children. Their happiness, confidence, and grounded outlook are immediately apparent to all who visit.
Thorngrove Nursery is a truly special place—where children are free to be themselves, and their unique spark is recognised, nurtured, and encouraged to shine.

Academic Life
What's in this section?
At Thorngrove School, academic life is considered one of the most important areas, with a commitment to providing an education that enables all children to develop their full intellectual, physical, aesthetic, creative, emotional, spiritual, and social potential. The school aims to foster skilled, independent learners with an intellectual curiosity that will equip them for future life. Pupils are encouraged to engage in the 'Learning Pit', a concept where they undertake challenging tasks to deepen their understanding of topic work, build their resilience and encourage them to be critical and collaborative thinkers.
Thorngrove School believes in inspiring children to love learning through an atmosphere of fun, exploration, and discovery in lessons led by well-qualified and experienced teachers. The curriculum is clearly structured to enable children to achieve within a stimulating, challenging, and supportive learning environment, promoting enthusiasm and enjoyment.
The school's curriculum follows the National Curriculum Framework alongside the requirements of ISEB. Thorngrove prepares children for senior school entrance exams, scholarships, and Common Entrance assessment. It offers a broad curriculum that prioritises a strong academic core of subjects, while also developing pupils' independent learning skills and resilience through motivating and supportive teaching.
Reading is central to the English Department's approach. The curriculum is built around high-quality texts, offering opportunities to explore important themes, different cultural settings, traditional and contemporary literature, language use, discussion, and reflection.
Each book acts as a "springboard" for developing essential speaking, listening, and comprehension skills, writing for various audiences and purposes, and improving spelling, punctuation, and grammar.
The school aims to develop a lifelong love of reading, fostering it through quality texts, enthusiastic teaching, competitions, a school reading dog, and special celebration days. It is believed that the more "technical" aspects of English come more easily when children enjoy lessons and are "hooked by a book".
Maths is seen as an integral part of life, with the aim for children to develop a solid foundation and the confidence to navigate their future journey. Pupils are encouraged to think through problems, review evidence, and arrive at conclusions, fostering confidence to learn from mistakes and build resilience.
The department promotes a positive relationship with maths, developing imagination and flexible thought.
Children are taught to work both independently and collaboratively, understanding how maths connects across subjects and its importance in life. Key skills and concepts are revisited and built upon year by year to deepen understanding.
A sound knowledge of Science is considered essential for all children to understand life in the 21st Century. Science encourages critical thinking, developing a "how and why" approach to look beyond basic facts, question assumptions, and identify patterns and consequences in data.
Understanding Science helps children appreciate and relate to the rapidly changing world. It teaches them to make observations, collect information, and draw conclusions by being reflective and observing closely. Mistakes are valued as learning opportunities in a safe environment.
The Science curriculum aims to capture students' curiosity through a wide range of exciting and challenging experiments and investigations. Practical teaching is emphasised as crucial for making Science accessible and enjoyable. Pupils are encouraged to take their love of Science out of the lab and into the real world.
Language learning is highly regarded. Children learn French from nursery up to the end of Year 8. While French is the primary language taught, Spanish and German can be offered as extra-curricular activities.
In Year 7, children participate in a week of "total immersion" in Normandy, France, staying at a purpose-built chateau. They are encouraged to speak French constantly and experience authentic French culture through activities like fencing, excursions to local markets, and a chocolate factory. This experience is valuable preparation for the listening and speaking parts of the French Common Entrance (CE) exams.

Welcome to
Pre-Prep
welcome to pre-prep from
our Head of Lower School
"My two daughters and I began our Thorngrove adventure together in 2013, and just two years later, I had the privilege of becoming Head of Pre-Prep—known to us as the Lower School. If anyone asks, I will always say I have the best job in the school!
In Lower School, we are a team of like-minded, passionate educators dedicated to making each child’s experience truly exceptional. We wholeheartedly believe that children learn best in a kind, calm, and supportive environment - where resilience is second nature and there’s no such thing as failure, only opportunities to learn and grow.
Walk into any classroom, and you’ll find smiles, laughter, and a genuine sense of belonging. Here, everyone is known, valued, and cared for. The sense of family is real and deeply felt - it’s far more than just a hashtag.
Our purpose-built classrooms open directly onto age-appropriate outdoor learning spaces, and yes - waterproof boiler suits are a must! We head outside in all weathers because learning at Thorngrove doesn’t stop at the classroom door.
Children in the Lower School benefit from an enriched curriculum delivered by specialist teachers in Forest School, Music, Drama, ICT, Ballet, French, and PE - all using the same high-quality resources as our older pupils. Daily sessions in Anima Phonics and mathematics help build strong foundations, while themed topic days bring learning to life in the most engaging and memorable ways.
Thorngrove Lower School — Simply the best!"
Find out more about life in Lower School -
Lower School Life

SEE FOR YOURSELF
BOOK A TOUR
Come and visit us in Lower School and see first-hand how we help every child to reach for the stars by planting strong roots from the very start.
our AIMS
Be Curious
Curiosity is at the heart of learning. We provide consistently excellent and exciting teaching which enables every pupil to develop intellectual enquiry. Our aim is to ignite and nurture a lifelong love of learning. These efforts build upon our unchanged founding pillars: Inspiration, Confidence, and Achievement
Be Community-Minded
Encouraging sensitivity and empathy is key to our approach. We help pupils develop these qualities towards those around them and in the wider world. Additionally, we actively promote well-being, mindfulness, and a strong sense of worth in all our pupils.
Be Challenged
At Thorngrove, we are dedicated to helping every child achieve their full potential. This means maximising academic results in all internal, standardised, and external examinations. Beyond academics, we focus on building resilience and promoting a positive mind-set among all our pupils.
Be Creative
We believe in enabling pupils, regardless of their ability, to discover and develop their individual talents. This includes a wide range of activities such as Sport, the Performing and Creative Arts, and other enriching pursuits. Our goal is to provide opportunities for every child to shine.
“A wide range of extra-curricular activities provide pupils with enjoyable and meaningful learning experiences. This is a significant strength of the school. Pupils across the school thrive during weekly lessons in the woods, which support their physical, mental and emotional wellbeing through effective teaching.”

“Pupils across the school are articulate. They express their ideas and discuss their learning confidently. The calm and purposeful atmosphere around the school is strengthened by pupils’ respectful relationships between staff and each other.”
“Pupils acquire new knowledge and understanding because of effective teaching.”

We know no limits
Treloar’s is a charity that provides outstanding education, therapy and care to physically disabled young people, and empowers them to live more independent and fulfilling lives.
A world where physically disabled young people take control of their lives and achieve their aspirations.
Who we support
We provide education and individual learning pathways, health care and therapy support to children with physical needs.
How we do it
We have over 800 expert staff – teachers, physiotherapists, nurses and more, providing wrap around support to our students.
Our outcomes
We educate 170 students from 23 counties across the UK and Ireland and help them to lead individual and fulfilling lives.
Job opportunities at Treloar's

Support Us
Treloar's is a charity which runs one of the UK's largest specialist education centres for young disabled people to live and learn.
Our highly specialist staff deliver outstanding education, therapy and care for our students. But we need your support to do so much more. It is essential that we raise £2 million every year, in addition to the funding we receive from Local Authorities.

Parent and Carer's Handbook
The Parent and Carer Handbook provides essential information about our routines, expectations, and ways to support your child. Whether you need guidance on attendance, school events, or curriculum insights, these pages are designed to help.
Welcome to Treloar’s ​
"At Treloar’s, we believe in the power of education. Our student-centred, holistic approach integrates on-site learning, residential care, pastoral support, therapy, and healthcare, ensuring a well-rounded experience tailored to each child's unique needs.
"Each student receives a curriculum that is right, relevant and purposeful, tailored to their unique needs and starting point. Our focus extends beyond the academic to include the development of resilience, determination, self-advocacy, and independence as students prepare for the next stage in their lives. ​ ​
"Treloar’s success is built on collaboration and teamwork and not accepting commonly recognised limitations and barriers. We value strong partnerships between school and home and encourage you to connect with us through parent-teacher meetings, events or the parent portal. Together, we can ensure that Treloar’s remains a place where children with physical disabilities flourish and succeed."​
Lisa Bond, Head of School​
"This is a school with great purpose and endless compassion."
Ofsted School Education Inspection Feb 24
How to get in touch
We believe that strong communication between parents, carers and staff is vital to support your child's education and wellbeing. ​
​Main Switchboard 01420 547400 ​(Mon-Fri 8.30am – 5pm) ​
Out of Hours Duty Manager 07736 080 220 ​
Safeguarding Manager 07825 262418 ​
Admissions Office 01420 547747
Report a student absence 01420 547402 ​
Emergency contact ​
Please ensure emergency contact details are updated regularly, our admin team will send you requests annually please can we ask you complete this as soon as possible. Please always provide us with two emergency contacts. It is vitally important that you notify us of any changes, as soon as possible.
School day​
Arrival: 8:50 am – 9:00 am ​
Break: 10:30 am – 11:15 am ​
Lunch: 12:30 pm – 2:00 pm ​
End of day: Primary: 3:30 pm Secondary: 4.00 pm Friday afternoon: 3.30 pm for Primary and Secondary students
Arrival on site​
Treloar Reception is in the Jowett Centre. On arrival all visitors, including parents and carers, must go directly to Reception and sign-in, where a visitors’ badge will be issued. All visitors to the site will need to be escorted by a member of staff at all times, even if you are familiar with our site. Please do not use mobile phones in school learning environments​​. These procedures are in place to ensure the safety of our students and staff.
Student ID badges ​
Students are issued with ID badges which allow independent access to the school buildings. Badges are issued to students when they arrive each morning and are handed back in at the end of the day. ​
Vehicle access and parking ​
Parents/carers must register their vehicle registration details to obtain access to the site via the security barrier, situated at the end of the drive. You can park in the visitor’s car park and walk to the Jowett Centre reception where you will be able to drop off and collect your child. The main car park is at the rear of the site and the Jowett Centre is signposted from there.
Please note that we have a lot of day students with different transport arrangements. We aim to ensure the process is as smooth and efficient as possible but there may be delays during drop off and pick up times. ​
Transport arrangements ​​
Local Authority transport​
You will need to liaise and apply directly to your Local Authority for school transport. Please contact your Student Progress Coordinator (SPC) if you need support with this. ​
If your child receives Local Authority transport, please provide us with the contact details for our records. ​
Parent / Carer transport:​
You can park in the visitor’s car park and walk to the Jowett Centre reception where you will be able to collect your child at 3.30pm for Primary and 4.00pm for Secondary. ​
Please note that we have a lot of day students with different transport arrangements. We aim to ensure the process is as smooth and efficient as possible but there may be delays on some occasions. ​
Drop off and pick up times ​
Students can be dropped off by Local Authority transport or parents. Students with their families/ transport escorts can wait under the shelter at the entrance to the Jowett Centre. Doors will be open from 8.50am. In adverse weather please can we ask that students do not queue. ​
At 8:50am staff will meet students and take them into school to sign-in and get ready for the school day. ​
Students will be brought back to the Jowett Centre at 3.30pm for Primary and 4.00pm for Secondary where they will be handed over to parents or Local Authority transport company. ​
"Treloar’s is a network of expertise and support that we never take for granted and which gives our son a wide range of opportunities for growth and development."
Parent / carer survey, Summer 2024
Unexpected school closure​
If the school needs to close at short notice (e.g. in the event of bad weather) we will inform all parents/carers and you will need to make arrangements to collect your child immediately. ​
In the event of an emergency e.g., Infectious disease outbreak or severe weather warning, Treloar’s will instigate the following contingency plan for the effective removal of students and staff from the site as quickly as possible: ​
You will be contacted by text and email ​
Within 3 hours of receiving the message you should notify us by telephone the proposed arrangements and time for your son/daughter’s departure from school ​
Please note, that due to the vulnerability of our students (and for some, the long distances involved in travelling) it is possible that Treloar’s unexpected closure measures e.g. infectious disease or severe weather, will be put in place ahead of your local mainstream schools and colleges. ​
Attendance / absence ​
Attendance is recorded for the morning and afternoon sessions. The information is available for the Department of Education (DFE) to view daily. Attendance data is also reported through your child’s Annual Review and shared with the Local Authority at their request. ​​
If your son or daughter is not well enough to attend school, please contact the school office immediately via phone (01420 547402) or email school.office@treloar.org.uk. ​
Parents will be contacted if a student does not arrive to school and the School Office have not been notified. Please note that even if you have liaised with another member of staff, you must still notify the office directly. ​​
Medical appointments ​
Medical appointments should be made, where possible, in the school holidays. We are aware that sometimes this will not be possible. Please notify the school office of any upcoming appointments and provide the hospital letter. Your child’s multi-disciplinary team and Treloar Health Centre will be notified. ​
Please let the Health Centre administration team know about any appointments, test results and consultant reports. Please send this to medical.secretary@treloar.org.uk ​
Returning to school after a period of illness ​
All students who have been absent and unwell for 7 days or more will require a reassessment before returning. Your child’s Student Progress Coordinator (SPC) will coordinate this. In some instances, this may simply be a telephone call home​
Since the education, therapy and care we provide is based on the initial assessment of a young person’s needs, we need to know if things change. If we have advance warning, we can make amendments to individual care plans, staff training or arrange additional support. If we are not appropriately prepared, we sometimes have to delay students’ return. We therefore ask that you alert us as soon as possible to any changes. ​
Your Student Progress Co-ordinator (SPC) needs to know if there has been:​
A need for an assessment in hospital or urgent care centre (even if not as an inpatient)​
An admission to hospital e.g., for illness or surgery​
Absence due to illness lasting more than 7 days​
In these cases, we will need to re-assess your young person. This will be arranged as a priority at your convenience and may range from a simple phone call to an onsite MDT assessment. We are unable to accept a returning student unless this process has been followed; please be assured we agree the vast majority of students to return straight after the reassessment.
In other instances, for example after surgery or a hospital admission, it may be necessary for you to attend an onsite reassessment with your child and their multi-disciplinary team. It is expected that you will take your child home after the reassessment. Your SPC will be in contact to advise of a return date. ​​
The reassessment of your child is to ensure we capture any change in needs that may impact on changes to daily care plans, medication, training needs for staff, equipment changes, particularly where any of these result in an increase of staffing and/or funding. ​​
After any hospital admission we require a discharge summary from the hospital in advance of reassessment. ​​
Please advise your child’s SPC as soon as you are aware of upcoming surgery. ​
Exceptional Leave of Absence ​
It is expected that any holidays will be taken within the school holidays, please refer to term dates online. Please contact the Head of School if there are any extenuating exceptional circumstances where a holiday/time away from school cannot be taken within these times.​
Who will work with my child? ​
Every child has an onsite multi-disciplinary team (MDT). ​​
The MDT is coordinated by your child’s allocated Student Progress Coordinator (SPC). As part of the MDT your child will have a named teacher, physiotherapist, occupational therapist, speech and language therapist, primary care lead, nurse and a student progress coordinator.
​​This team will meet regularly to review your child's achievement and progress and ensure that they are reaching their maximum potential. Priority will be given to developing their communication skills, together with developing their personal independence and physical wellbeing. The wider MDT available as needed can also include dietitian, assistive technology technician and counsellors. ​
The SPC will also be your main point of contact at Treloar’s. They will support you and your child through their journey at Treloar’s with a particular focus on transition points i.e., Primary to Secondary transfer. They will be the key contact for external agencies too, e.g. social services. ​​
In Primary we have a team of specialists (Primary care leads) that support your child’s pastoral needs focussing on care, nutrition and medical needs during the school day. This team work as part of your child’s MDT and work closely with the health centre and education department to implement systems of support to enable your child’s education. This team is set up similarly to the care teams on residential houses that will take over this role as your child moves into secondary. ​​
If your child has a home care team: ​
We will link in and share information with home care teams to ensure consistency and collaboration. The frequency of these will be arranged with your child’s class teacher and student progress coordinator. Where requested we will invite home care practitioners/teams to attend the Annual Review of EHCP. ​
"My daughter...is being seen for who she is and not a condition."
Parent / carer survey Summer 2024
School uniform
The comfort of our students is our priority, and this is also necessary to ensure they are ready to learn. For some students clothing can be uncomfortable with scratchy seams and labels or tight waistbands. We have a flexible uniform so parents can adapt clothing items to meet their child’s needs.The school uniform is:
Treloar’s uniform can be purchased online from Skoolkit or telephone 02380 651278
Black trousers/tracksuit bottoms/ skirt
What does my child need to bring to school?
To support your child to access every opportunity across the school day we also require that your child has: ​
Medication (correct prescription label and in date)​
Communication equipment
Medical devices – suction machine, cough assist, if your child has a prescription for medication it is essential they are bought into school each day – failure to do so may result in you needing to collect your child ​
Shoes/boots - to access their physiotherapy equipment ​
Backpack to carry items between home and school ​
Swimming costume, towel and continence swimwear​
Weather dependent items ​- For colder weather: warm anorak or coat, blankets, gloves and hats. For warmer weather: hat and sun cream ​
Care items and continence products​​
A minimum of one set of spare clothes
Meals and snacks
All meals are provided by Treloar’s, catering for a range of textures and specific dietary requirements. Only food produced by our kitchens can be consumed in the dining rooms. Any additional snack items sent in must be in sealed, commercially prepared packaging with ingredients and allergens clearly listed. Requests outside of these policies must be discussed with the dietitian at the time of assessment and, if agreed, parameters/risk assessment documented prior to being sent in.
Equipment
Please ensure that all equipment is appropriately insured. Wheelchair users should have third party indemnity insurance.Please find below information on some of the equipment that your child may use and bring to school:
If your child does not have a headrest or anti-tip bars, please contact your local Wheelchair Service. If you need any support, please contact the Treloar’s Physio Team.

Join us for our Recruitment Open Evening on Tuesday 29th September 2026
Community access for primary students
Thanks to £3,300 in Councillor Grants from East Hampshire District Councillors, Treloar’s has purchased a specialist Baffin Simon car seat, helping students safely access educational trips and community activities.
Thanks to valuable support from East Hampshire Councillors, we have been able to purchase a Baffin Simon specialist car seat. This will be used by primary school students to enable them to access the wider community for educational purposes as well as for leisure activities. Not only are trips fun, they are also vital for learning essential life skills and extending enriched learning beyond the classroom.
Thank you to Cllr Graham Hill, Cllr Elizabeth Marshall, Cllr Emily Young, Cllr Suzie Burns, and Cllr Barbara Tansey from East Hampshire District Council for contributing a total of £3,300 from their Councillor Grants.
Current safety guidance recommends that children weighing under 22kg travel in an appropriate 5-point harness car seat rather than in a wheelchair. However, standard child car seats often do not provide the level of postural support required by many of our students, making it challenging to ensure their safety and comfort during transport.
After assessing different seats our Occupational Therapy department chose the Baffin seat as it is the most appropriate and adaptable for the wide needs of our students. The Simon car seat was specifically designed, so that every child using it can feel safe and comfortable and take the most comfortable position during the journey.
We need to raise a further £3,600 for a second car seat, to ensure that all classes are able to go out on a trip together. If you are able to contribute to this, or other fundraising requests, please contact the fundraising team on fundraising@treloars.org.uk. Thank you.

pageCache.text:
Welcome to Walhampton
A Truly Remarkable School
Walhampton lies in beautiful ancient woodland on the edge of the New Forest, near Lymington in Hampshire. A private day and boarding school for boys and girls aged 2-13, we strive to let children be children for longer, whilst preparing them for the unknown challenges and opportunities in the world of tomorrow.
Our stunning setting in 100 acres of lawns, lakes and woodland by the sea, means the children are inspired by nature whilst immersing themselves in limitless academic, artistic, technological, challenging and sporting experiences.
Our Head
A radical traditional educator
We are Walhampton
Discover the Walhampton magic
Pre-Prep
Growing the joy of learning
Prep
Developing curious, 21st century learners
Boarding
Making boarding home-from-home
2025 Shortlist Award
Walhampton shortlisted for Tes Independent Prep School of the Year
Join us
Start your admissions journey here
Latest News
Founders' Day 2026
Saturday 4th July saw the Walhampton community come together for our 2026 Founders' Day. A remarkable celebration of the 2025/26 academic year and especially poignant as we bid farewell to our Year 8 leavers.
Walhampton Early Years Update
As part of our long-term strategy to strengthen and evolve our provision for families, Walhampton Nursery will move to a year-round model from January 2027, operating for 48 weeks of the year for pre-school children aged two to four.
Curly Wurly Mountain
When you’ve run up the path that curls around the hill, or scampered through the Cherry Laurel hedges, you are rewarded with magnificent views across the grounds to the main house. A popular spot from Nursery to Year 8. Often used as a base during Flags – a Walhampton tradition played in the woods by all year groups in the Prep school. The children need to develop the sharpest strategies and tactics and then display determination and speed to win the day!
Stables
Our equestrian centre, complete with a multi-purpose manège, is home to a variety of horses and ponies of different heights, ages and abilities. All the ponies belong to individual pupils and are kept at school on working livery contracts, meaning they can be ridden by other pupils. From the most perfect Shetland pony for the smaller rider to Welsh and New Forest Ponies who have fantastic temperaments to ex competition horses for the more advanced riders – all the ponies are part of the Walhampton community and loved dearly.
Lake
This is one of three lakes at Walhampton and this one is predominantly used for kayaking. There is also a co-curricular fishing club and regular pond dipping sessions for outdoor learning and science lessons.
Swimming Pool
We have a 17m heated outdoor pool, which is used during the summer term and sometimes in September. As well as weekly swimming lessons and regular swimming galas, the pool is also used by boarders at the weekend and for an after school activity.
Remembrance Garden
Our Garden of Remembrance was created in 2016 to honour those men and women who endured the bloody battle of Arnhem, in Holland, in September 1944. Within the garden is a beautiful statue depicting a veteran standing alongside two school children carrying sunflowers. This was designed and sculpted by our Head of Art, Jane Pickance, who visited Arnhem as part of a Walhampton school trip and experienced first-hand the special relationship between the school and the veterans.
Sports Field
Sport plays an integral and important role at Walhampton. The combination of qualified staff and fantastic facilities provides outstanding opportunities for the pupils to learn, improve and develop their skills in a wide variety of different sports. Our lower sports field is predominantly used for rugby, football, cricket and athletics. It is large enough to host the Wessex Junior Athletics Championship every summer, with 20 schools taking part.
Main House
As well as classrooms and offices, within the main house is Bradfield House, our boarding house. The girls’ dormitories and common room are on the first floor and boys’ dormitories and common room are on the second floor with views across to the Isle of Wight. Our Heads of Boarding and Assistant House Parents all live in flats within Bradfield House, which helps create the ‘home from home’ environment that our boarders thrive in. Our dormitories were described by Tatler as “some of the best we’ve seen”.
Faraway Tree
Named after the Enid Blyton novels, The Faraway Tree is encased in climbing equipment on the front lawn and is a popular spot at break times.
Sports Hall
Our purpose-built sports hall with viewing gallery and a range of equipment, is just part of the suite of sports facilities at Walhampton. Our 100-acre grounds are put to good use and we have ample room on-site to accommodate a wide range of sports including three netball courts, a full-size Astroturf pitch, an outdoor heated pool, riding stables, a sailing lake, games pitches for rugby, football and cricket and an athletics track.
Netball
Walhampton has three outdoor netball courts as well as room to play indoors in the Sports Hall. The girls play netball during the Spring term and we often host an annual tournament with other Prep schools in the area.
Kitchen Garden
There’s a purposeful feel to the kitchen garden, particularly when there are raspberries or pears to pick. Throughout the year keen pupils help to weed, plant, stake and sample a range of organically grown fruit, vegetables and herbs from tomatoes, broad beans, runner beans, strawberries, potatoes, onions, rhubarb, to more unusual plants like okra, mini kiwi and cucamelons. The most popular activity is probably watering – we have a huge collection of watering cans, pupils have a ‘splashing’ time and most of the water ends up where it should!
Clock House
The Clock House is home to our two recently renovated science labs and the computing suite. The two science labs have everything we need for lots of hands-on learning. The science garden is a new outdoor learning space behind the labs. Nextdoor is our fully-equipped computer suite, packed with computers and a bank of Chromebooks. This is also home to our STAG Radio podcast recording studio.
Pre-Prep
Our self-contained, purpose-built Pre-Prep school was created with the children in mind: it is separate from the potentially daunting surroundings of ‘big school’ but adjacent to it too, so youngsters can easily access facilities including the Chapel, stables, swimming pool, library, ICT, music, performing arts centre, cookery kitchen and all that our 100 acre grounds have to offer. Vibrant classrooms have free-flow access to thoughtfully designed outdoor areas.
Outdoor Classroom
We have an outdoor classroom set in the woods within the grounds, which is used as often as possible by children of all ages for lessons, spanning from science to reading. There is a fire pit to keep warm in winter and a canopy to provide shade in summer, with seats and a blackboard to hold attention. This area is only part of the school’s focus on learning outdoors, with many lessons taking place elsewhere in the large grounds.
Forest School
Our Pre-Prep classes have weekly Forest School sessions which take place in our grounds, predominantly in our Forest School site in the woods near Portmore Lake. The benefits of Forest School extend beyond pure nature. Forest school activities complement and extend the academic curriculum. Children develop resilience, perseverance and determination to succeed as they work. These values are then transferred to the classroom and directly support their literacy, numeracy and other academic development.
Bee Hives
Every summer term pupils are invited to join our ever-popular beekeeping club. Our beekeeping expert teaches the children about feeding, hive construction and maintenance. And everyone enjoys the honey produced in our hives. A buzzy time!
Caravan
The gypsy caravan, which lives on the Front Lawn, was originally bought by Walhampton’s first headmaster, John Bradfield (JB) in the 1960s and used to take the boys camping in the New Forest along with other horse-drawn caravans. It is now owned by old Walhamptonian Lord Montagu of Beaulieu and kindly on loan for the pupils to play in.
Cricket Nets
The sound of leather of willow fills the air at Walhampton during the summer term with both boys and girls playing as their main sports.
Chapel
At its heart, Walhampton has a gentle, inclusive and meaningful Christian ethos. A number of engaging services and acts of worship occur each week in our beautiful chapel.
Visit Us
If you would like to experience Walhampton for yourself, please contact us, or visit us on one of our open mornings.

LEARNING SUPPORT
LEARNING SUPPORT
Not everyone learns at the same pace, but at Walhampton we support each pupil to ensure that no one gets left behind. For those children who need that little bit of extra input with lessons and understanding, our Learning Support Unit is there to help. The LSU team does a vital job and is an integral part of the school, with dedicated classrooms dotted all around the site, close to the other classrooms.
We work hard to ensure that the successes of every child are celebrated by the whole school. As a result, the children who receive learning support are confident and always make up a significant proportion of the school leadership positions. In recent years our Head Boy and Head Girl positions have been awarded to children with learning difficulties.
Walhampton’s team of specialist teachers deliver individual support to those who need it. Our aim is to nurture the children and instill confidence so they progress in their education. We absolutely believe that with the right support, every child can fulfil their true potential and we take joy in supporting each child in their growth and development.
We devise specific learning programmes for each child, focusing on particular areas of need - whether it be dyslexia, dyscalculia, or support with fine motor skills. The department is fortunate to have a wide selection of dyslexia-friendly books for all ages and fun resources which make our lessons stimulating and engaging.

SPORTS FOR ALL
SPORTS
Amidst a busy and stretching academic curriculum, sport brings an essential, invigorating balance and variety to daily school life. Our guiding principle is to create healthy minds and healthy bodies. Enjoyment of sport and an active outdoor lifestyle is encouraged at all skill levels. Every day we see the positive benefit of this approach, not least in how playing with and against other children fosters teamwork, confidence, and competitiveness.
Sport is timetabled for most days and is taught in groups of Years 3 and 4, 5 and 6, and 7 and 8. We arrange a comprehensive fixture list, either against other private schools or for inter-house competitions, and each week Walhampton fields up to 24 teams. Our sports include football, hockey, rugby, netball, cross country, cricket, athletics, rounders and swimming. As well as these more traditional sports, our pupils also compete in riding and sailing competitions.
Best You Can Be
In recent years, the senior girls have requested to play solely cricket in the Summer Term, rather than rounders as well. This move to cricket was driven by the pupils, who wanted to devote more time to this challenging game. This seems to have paid off: very successful seasons have followed as a result.
As in any subject, sport needs expert tuition if we are to bring out the best in people. That’s why Walhampton invests in a team of specialist coaches to help children develop the skills needed to participate effectively in their chosen sport. And although we all love to win, not everyone can be brilliant, not all teams will be successful, so along the way coaches also help every child to cope with Kipling’s two impostors, Triumph and Disaster. What matters is doing your very best.
RUN TO PERFORM
Most sports need space, and our 100-acre grounds are put to good use. We have ample room on-site to accommodate a wide range of facilities including three purpose-built netball courts, a full-size Astroturf pitch, an outdoor heated pool, a purpose-built sports hall, riding stables, a sailing lake, games pitches for rugby, football and cricket and an athletics track (that hosts the Junior Wessex Athletics Championships, with 26 leading schools from across the Wessex region).
Unsurprisingly, we also have numerous cross-country routes, offering different types of challenge and conditions, around our three lakes and well-stocked woods. We recently celebrated 42 years of our annual Perry Dalziell cross country race when we hosted 15 local primary schools in a great competition.
RUGBY AND NETBALL ACADEMIES
Walhampton’s Sports Academies offer an additional high level of coaching for promising pupils in the Seniors. As an extension to the core sports for all programme, children with sporting potential and a particular interest in Netball and Rugby can accelerate their learning and understanding of the game.
In addition to the weekly Academy training sessions with qualified and experienced coaches, dedicated pupils take part in half termly matches; enjoy an annual trip to watch and learn from a professional game; and benefit from a sport specific strength & conditioning sessions.
Do you know what my favourite part of the game is? The opportunity to play.

ARTS
ARTS
ART
As you’d expect, the Walhampton Art department is a hotbed of ideas and innovation, an active and vibrant area where the environment encourages creativity and is accessible for all children.
The school art rooms are large and well-equipped, allowing the children to work in a range of different materials and scales. (Keeping things clean and tidy is another challenge.)
Creativity doesn’t always work to a timetable, so children have the opportunity to get involved in all elements of the art department through after school clubs, enrichments and some break times. Our gifted art scholars enjoy further opportunities to express creativity through the scholarship program.
DRAMA
At Walhampton Drama, it all begins in Pre Prep with our Nativities, continuing through the Prep School where every pupil takes part in at least three productions, on the stage—plus our senior STRETCH show.
Rooted in Kindness, Curiosity and Achievement, our productions are all about creativity and teamwork. These times are truly special because every role is carefully shaped to help each child grow. I encourage pupils to be brave and step outside their comfort zones, with wonderful support from our senior drama scholars.
As a Green Flag school, we create productions sustainably, with plenty of shared fun from the Walhampton Community (big shout out to you wonderful volunteers!) in set-building and prop-making.
We also offer a drama scholarship pathway, alongside LAMDA lessons from Year 4 with regular exams.
MUSIC
Children from Nursery upwards enjoy music lessons in our recently developed music centre. As well as weekly class lessons, over 60% of pupils in Years 2 to 8 learn at least one instrument.
All styles of music are encouraged, and we have groups for all levels to get involved in orchestras, rock bands, jazz groups, three choirs and musical theatre. There are several opportunities to perform throughout the year, most are within the school but our musicians and choirs get an opportunity to perform at a local music festival and competition. Our Chapel Choir (which includes more than 50 pupils) also enjoys being invited to Limewood Hotel every Christmas to sing carols for guests.
Every other year, we celebrate the arts at the Walhampton School Arts Festival. Every child in the school takes part, with performances and exhibitions in the grounds and an afternoon of packed entertainment on a festival stage on the front lawn.
Every child is an artist. The problem is how to remain an artist once we grow up.

pageCache.pageTitle: Outdoor Learning & Forest School - Walhampton School
pageCache.text:
OUTDOOR LEARNING
OUTDOOR LEARNING
When you think of a school classroom, you’ll probably picture four walls, chairs and desks. But what if a classroom had none of that? Just trees and foliage, lakes and fields, open sky for a ceiling, and learning materials strewn around on the woodland floor. Now imagine how much fun that would be for any enquiring young mind.
That sort of experience is just one of the benefits that Walhampton brings to a child’s education. Nestled within its 100-acre grounds, the school has a Forest School site and an outdoor classroom, providing unrivalled opportunities for practical open-air learning.
Outdoor learning is increasingly embedded in all areas of the curriculum and year groups, with Years 3 to 5 now having weekly sessions timetabled.
By exploring nature and working together – doing things like climbing, collecting, shelter building, cooking and fire lighting – the children have opportunities to make independent choices and take risks in a safe and controlled environment.
Children are natural-born adventurers and want to learn anything and everything about the world around them, so it is important that schools help them do this. This can help them to develop early approaches to problem-solving and year on year Walhampton sees a significant boost in self-awareness, independence, motor skills, confidence and importantly at this time, well-being. The outdoor curriculum also ensures that children develop communication abilities through collaborative-working.
EXPEDITIONS
Expeditions Week is generally seen as one of the most important weeks of the school year and defines what Walhampton is all about.
We provide children with experiences outside the classroom which lead to greater confidence, self-reliance, selflessness and increased knowledge of how to be part of a team. Expeditions ‘week’ lasts for 5 to 7 days towards the end of the summer term and is an integral part of education at Walhampton, involving all the Prep children and staff. It is very different from anything else offered either on the curriculum, in games or activities, and deliberately so.
Expeditions Week is a natural extension of our outdoor learning provision. Read more about it on our Expeditions page.

PHYSICAL, SOCIAL, HEALTH AND ECONOMIC EDUCATION
Personal, Social, Health and Economic Education
Personal, Social, Health and Economic Education is the planned provision to promote the pupils’ personal, social and emotional development, as well as their health and wellbeing.
Through our teaching of PSHEE we aim to:
We believe that the personal, social and health development of each child has a significant role in their ability to learn and enjoy learning. We value the importance of PSHEE in preparing pupils for the opportunities, responsibilities and experiences of adult life. In addition, we believe that a child needs to learn about the many emotional aspects of life and how to manage their own emotions.
PSHEE also supports many of the principles of Safeguarding and helps the children understand how to stay safe. As part of Keeping Children Safe in Education (KCSIE) 2022 and noted in the School’s Safeguarding and Child Protection policy, staff have a duty to ensure the welfare of all children. In the PSHE curriculum, the children are taught how to be safe, secure, healthy, develop emotional resilience, promote self-esteem and develop their confidence which is an integral part of growing up.

KEY STAGE ONE
KEY STAGE ONE
As children move into Key Stage 1 at Walhampton, a broader and deeper curriculum is introduced. We work hard to encourage independent thinking, taking a questioning approach to learning as well as preparing our children for the future – all within a nurturing environment.
KEY STAGE 1 – YEAR ONE
In Year 1, children move from the Early Years Foundation Stage to the National Curriculum. This transition is managed with great care as we dove-tail the end of Reception with the beginning of Year 1.
This is a year to take on new responsibilities and gain a greater awareness of each other and the world around us. Creative teaching with a topic-based approach, stimulates children with new ideas and fosters a sense of purpose. At the same time, structured play and role-playing reinforces the academic goals and ideas being explored in lessons.
Weekly visits to Forest School and other outdoor learning opportunities provide the perfect environment to develop and apply the key characteristics of learning (resilience, risk-taking, initiative, curiosity, originality and empathy).
KEY STAGE ONE – YEAR TWO
In Year 2 the children are more aware of their abilities and increasingly proud of academic achievements. We start to gently introduce learning strategies, such as memory maps, which the children can build on as they continue through school. This includes helping individuals to become more confident and independently minded throughout their learning, general behaviour and friendship circles. We also promote greater independence and organisational skills, particularly in the morning and end-of-day routines.
With strong foundations in place, Year 2 is the time to further stretch the children academically, with an even broader integrated curriculum, whilst continuing to ensure that learning is tailored to meet the needs of each individual child.

EARLY YEARS
Our Nursery, Kindergarten and Reception classes provide an inspirational setting for children to start their academic journey from two to five years old. This was reflected in our latest report from the Independent Schools Inspectorate.
WHAT WE OFFER
We pride ourselves on an Early Years provision that combines high-quality education with genuine flexibility, designed to support both children and families at every stage. Children join us from the age of two, with funding options available, full-time places across all classes and extended provision throughout the day and year. Our children benefit from experienced staff who know them well, creating a strong sense of security and continuity.
From January 2027 our provision is strengthening as we move to a year-round model, operating for 48 weeks of the year for pre-school children aged two-four.

NURSERY AND STEPPING STONES
From two years of age, children are welcomed into our Nursery, a warm, happy and nurturing environment. Our door is always open so parents can share ideas, ask questions and help ensure their children feel safe and happy. Our Nursery approach covers all areas of child development - social, creative and physical. These areas are developed through purposeful play, both inside and out, as the children embark upon the Early Years Foundation Stage (EYFS) curriculum.
